comments.text:
I own this one. At one point, this was a decent card. It was 20 bucks more than the GeForce GT 1030 new and offered about 2x the performance, which was good (for a new card, used there are obviously much better deals, at least back in the day, and today there still are better used deals). I will say though, the fact that your particularly card requires a 6-pin power connector greatly defeats its purpose. 

For those with weaker power supplies that don't have any extra connections, such as those with minitower Dell Optiplexes (whom SHOULD be the audience for these kinds of cards, as there are plenty of better choices even today if one's power supply can support extra connections/has the wattage for it), their best option is a GeForce GTX 1650, followed by the GeForce GTX 1050 TI, and as you've shown with your previous Sunday videos on those two cards, it's just doable enough for most contemporary purposes (barring everyone's favorite best-optimized game, Cyberpunk 2077).

However both of those cards, at least in the states, have gotten very expensive for their performance. The 1050 TI is usually $150+ used barring lucky bids (the price of one new... more than 3 years ago when it was released) and the 1650 often is used at above its retail price! Even the GeForce GTX 750 TI reaches $100+ regularly used. (I'm actually excited for the GeForce GT 1010. I'm curious to see the progression from the 210 ---> 710 ----> 1010!) It's sad to see the best (new) value is the $35 1 GB GDDR5 GT 710 I saw on Amazon a few weeks back. That's actually not too bad of a deal for something new, especially since 2 GB DDR3 are usually for $45-$50 (edit: I checked today and they're all gone! Nothing gets by these people!).

The RX 560 new was $100 and the 1050 TI was $140 and the 1050 TI offered about... 35-40% more performance. So they were right on level with each other for their price-performance. Compare that to 1050, which $10 more and offered about 10% more performance. So it was not a bad (new) option if budgets were tight (which if one was buying something like an old Optiplex, the budget probably was tight.)

I miss when prices were competitive. Anyway great Sunday video as always!
